description: How a processor, its memory hierarchy and its I/O system are organised and why they perform as they do: instruction sets, datapaths, pipelining, caches, virtual memory, superscalar and multicore design, with a simulated processor built and measured along the way. Taught to the depth of a leading computer architecture course.
modelledOn: Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design
Hennessy and Patterson, Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach (selected chapters)
outcomes: Measure and reason about performance with execution time, CPI, Amdahl's law and benchmarks.
Describe an instruction set architecture and trace instructions through a single-cycle and a multi-cycle datapath.
Design a pipelined processor and handle structural, data and control hazards with forwarding, stalls and branch prediction.
Analyse cache and virtual memory behaviour and compute hit rates, miss penalties and address translations.
Explain hardwired and microprogrammed control and superscalar, out-of-order and multicore execution.
Describe I/O organisation, interrupts, DMA and the interconnection structure of a modern system.

units.title: Computer evolution and performance
topics: Generations of computers; Moore's law, Dennard scaling and the end of frequency scaling
Performance metrics: execution time, throughput, clock rate, CPI, MIPS and their traps
Amdahl's law; benchmarks (SPEC) and performance comparison
Power, energy and cooling as design constraints; mobile versus server design points

units.title: Top-level view of function and interconnection
topics: Von Neumann architecture; the instruction cycle with interrupts
Buses: address, data, control; arbitration, timing, hierarchies
Point-to-point interconnects: QPI, PCIe, on-chip networks
Program execution traced at the register-transfer level

units.title: Instruction sets
topics: Machine instruction characteristics, operand types, data types, operations
Addressing modes and instruction formats; fixed versus variable length
RISC-V (or MIPS) as the running example: registers, loads and stores, arithmetic, branches, procedure calls, the stack
x86 and ARM compared; CISC versus RISC and the RISC argument
Translating C to assembly to machine code; the compiler, assembler, linker and loader
Floating point: IEEE 754 arithmetic in hardware

units.title: Processor structure and function: the datapath
topics: Register organisation, user-visible and control registers, flags
Building a single-cycle datapath: instruction fetch, register file, ALU, data memory, control signals
Multi-cycle datapath and finite-state control
Control unit operation: micro-operations, hardwired control design
Microprogrammed control: control memory, microinstruction formats, sequencing, horizontal versus vertical
Implementing the datapath in a simulator and tracing a program

units.title: Pipelining
topics: The five-stage pipeline; speedup and its limits; pipeline registers
Structural hazards; data hazards and forwarding; load-use stalls
Control hazards: stalling, delayed branches, static and dynamic branch prediction (BHT, BTB, two-bit predictors)
Exceptions and interrupts in a pipeline; precise exceptions
Deeper pipelines and their costs

units.title: Instruction-level parallelism, superscalar and RISC
topics: RISC characteristics revisited: register windows, compiler scheduling, large register files
Superscalar execution: multiple issue, instruction window, dependencies (true, anti, output)
Out-of-order execution: register renaming, Tomasulo's algorithm, reorder buffer, speculation
VLIW and the limits of ILP; Spectre-style side channels as a consequence of speculation

units.title: Cache memory and the memory hierarchy
topics: Locality and the memory hierarchy; SRAM versus DRAM; memory organisation and interleaving
Cache mapping: direct, set-associative, fully associative; block size, replacement policies, write policies
Multi-level caches; average memory access time; the three Cs of misses; cache-aware programming (matrix multiply)
Virtual memory: pages, page tables, TLBs, page faults; address translation worked examples; protection
Cache coherence in multiprocessors: snooping and MESI

units.title: Input/output
topics: I/O modules, programmed I/O, interrupt-driven I/O, direct memory access
I/O channels and processors; buses and interfaces: USB, PCIe, SATA, NVMe
Storage: magnetic disks, SSDs, RAID levels; reliability and availability
Interrupt handling and the operating system's view of devices

units.title: Parallel processing and multicore computers
topics: Flynn's taxonomy; SIMD and vector units; GPUs as throughput processors
Symmetric multiprocessors, NUMA, clusters; cache coherence and memory consistency
Multithreading: fine-grained, coarse-grained, simultaneous (hyper-threading)
Multicore organisation: shared caches, interconnects, heterogeneous cores (big.LITTLE in phones)
Parallel speed-up, Amdahl again, and writing a parallel program that scales

schedule.title: Computer evolution and performance
schedule.exercise: Problem set: compute CPI, execution time and MIPS for three programs on two machines, show why MIPS can mislead, and apply Amdahl's law to a 40 percent speed-up of one part.

tasks.title: Compute execution time from instruction count, CPI and clock rate for three programs on two machines and decide which machine is faster for each
Plot overall speed-up against the fraction of a program sped up by 10 times using Amdahl's law, and read off the fraction needed for a speed-up of 3
Compare a phone core and a server core on performance per watt from supplied figures, and decide which design suits a solar-powered field office

schedule.title: Von Neumann machine, buses and interconnects
schedule.exercise: Trace the fetch, decode, execute and interrupt phases of three instructions at register-transfer level, writing PC, MAR, MBR and IR values after every step.

tasks.title: Step through the fetch-decode-execute cycle for a load, an add and a store, and record the PC and accumulator after each instruction
Trace a four-instruction program at register-transfer level, writing the register and bus contents at each micro-step, and check them against the visualiser
Simulate two bus masters competing for one shared bus under fixed-priority and round-robin arbitration, and find which policy starves a device

schedule.title: Instruction sets and RISC-V
schedule.exercise: Write RISC-V assembly for an array sum and a recursive factorial, annotate each instruction's format and addressing mode, and trace the stack through the procedure calls.

tasks.title: Step through a six-instruction RISC-V program that adds two registers and stores the result, and note each register value
Encode ten RISC-V instructions into 32-bit machine words by hand, decode them in the visualiser, and identify the format of each
Write RISC-V code for a procedure that sums an array and calls a helper, and show the stack frame and return address at each call

schedule.title: ISAs compared, toolchain and floating point
schedule.exercise: Compile a short C function by hand into pseudo-assembly for a RISC and a CISC machine, count instructions and bytes, and write what the assembler and linker do next.

tasks.title: Convert 5.75 and -0.15625 into IEEE 754 single precision by hand and verify each bit pattern with the converter
Add two IEEE 754 numbers of different exponents step by step, showing alignment, addition and normalisation, and compare the result with the exact sum
Translate a small C loop to assembly, assemble it to machine words and load it, then trace its execution and count instructions executed

schedule.title: Registers and the datapath
schedule.exercise: Draw a single-cycle datapath with control signals for add, load, store and branch, and fill a table of control-signal values for each instruction type.

tasks.title: Run a short program in the register-level simulator and watch the flag register change after an add, a subtract and a compare
Set the control signals of a single-cycle datapath by hand for add, load, store and branch instructions, and confirm each runs correctly
Convert a single-cycle design into a multi-cycle design with a finite state controller, then compare cycles per instruction for a given program mix

schedule.title: Control unit design and microprogramming
schedule.exercise: Design a microprogram for three instructions with a horizontal and a vertical microinstruction format, and compare control-store size for each.

tasks.title: Step through the micro-operations of an add instruction in a hardwired control unit and name the control signals asserted in each cycle
Write microinstructions for load, add and branch in a small control store, run them in the visualiser, and verify the micro-program counter sequencing
Trace a supplied nine-instruction program on the simulated datapath, find the instruction whose control word is faulty, and correct it

schedule.title: Pipelining and hazards
schedule.exercise: Pipeline diagram exercise: draw the five-stage timing for a given ten-instruction sequence with and without forwarding, and count the stall cycles in each case.

tasks.title: Run five independent instructions through the five-stage pipeline and compute speed-up against a non-pipelined machine
Run a code sequence with data hazards, switch forwarding on and off, and count stall cycles caused by the load-use dependency
Compare static not-taken prediction with a two-bit predictor on a loop-heavy trace, and report misprediction rate and the cycles lost to each branch

schedule.title: Exceptions and deeper pipelines
schedule.exercise: Explain in a short note why exceptions are hard in a pipeline, and give an example where two instructions in flight both raise exceptions.

tasks.title: Trigger an arithmetic overflow exception in the pipeline simulator and note which instructions are flushed and which complete
Raise an exception in a middle instruction and verify the pipeline keeps a precise state, listing the registers that must be preserved
Compare a 5-stage and a 14-stage pipeline on a branch-heavy program using supplied stage delays, and decide where deeper stops helping

schedule.title: Superscalar, out-of-order and speculative execution
schedule.exercise: Classify every dependency (true, anti, output) in a given eight-instruction sequence and show which renamed registers remove the false ones.

tasks.title: Identify true, anti and output dependencies in a six-instruction code sequence and mark each on a dependency graph
Run a code sequence through Tomasulo's algorithm in the visualiser, tracking reservation stations, renaming and commit order from the reorder buffer
Walk through a bounds-check-bypass speculation example, show how a cache timing difference leaks a value, and propose two mitigations with their cost

schedule.title: Memory hierarchy and cache design
schedule.exercise: Problem set: for a 16 KB cache with given block size, split addresses into tag, index and offset, simulate 20 accesses, and compute the hit rate and average access time.

tasks.title: Simulate a direct-mapped cache on 16 given addresses and mark each as a hit or a miss with the reason
Run the same address trace on direct-mapped and 4-way caches with LRU replacement and compare hit rates and the conflict misses removed
Tune a blocked matrix multiplication by choosing a tile size against a simulated two-level cache, and minimise average memory access time

schedule.title: Virtual memory and cache coherence
schedule.exercise: Worked examples: translate five virtual addresses with a two-level page table and a TLB, noting hits, misses and page faults, then explain the protection check.

tasks.title: Translate six virtual addresses to physical addresses with a single-level page table and mark each TLB hit, miss or page fault
Trace twelve memory references through a TLB and two-level page table with a limited frame pool and count page faults under FIFO replacement
Trace a MESI protocol with three cores reading and writing one shared line, record each state change, and count the bus transactions needed

schedule.title: Input/output, storage and RAID
schedule.exercise: Compare programmed I/O, interrupt-driven I/O and DMA for moving a 4 KB block, with a table of CPU cycles used by each approach.

tasks.title: Transfer a block of 64 bytes with programmed I/O and with DMA, and compare the number of CPU cycles spent on each
Compute usable capacity, fault tolerance and write cost for RAID 0, 1, 5 and 6 on six 2 TB disks, and tabulate the results
Handle a burst of device interrupts with nested priorities and a limited stack, and find the interrupt-masking policy that avoids lost events

schedule.title: Parallel processing and multicore
schedule.exercise: Short report: for a program with a measured serial fraction, predict speed-up on 2, 4, 8 and 16 cores with Amdahl's law and explain why real runs fall short.

tasks.title: Classify ten processors and workloads into SISD, SIMD, MISD or MIMD, and run a vector add on a simulated SIMD unit
Compare coarse-grained, fine-grained and simultaneous multithreading on a program with long memory stalls and compute the utilisation of the issue slots
Write a parallel sum with threads, measure speed-up on 1 to 8 workers, and explain the gap from ideal speed-up using measured overheads
